summary: A median age of 19.2 and a population that is 97.2 percent between 18 and 34 — this is not a town in any conventional sense but essentially the residential footprint of Cal Poly San Luis Obispo's campus, a 1.5-square-mile census-designated place where nearly every resident is a university student. That context reframes every other number: the $518,800 median home value reflects a narrow stock of properties largely purchased as rentals or by the university itself, not a market most occupants are participating in as buyers. The 73.8 percent bachelor's-degree rate is almost certainly an artifact of graduate students and recent completers still counted in the population rather than a signal of a settled professional class. Daily life here is shaped by the volcanic morros and rolling Irish-green hills of the Central Coast — campus sits against the dramatic backdrop of Cerro San Luis and Bishop Peak, with trailheads reachable on foot. The 9.6 hours of daily sunshine and an average high of 69°F make for remarkably temperate conditions year-round, rarely too hot or too cold. San Luis Obispo proper, just adjacent, supplies the downtown restaurants, Thursday farmers' market, and daily errands that this tiny CDP lacks on its own. The defining reality is that this is a place calibrated almost entirely around one institution — its rhythms, its calendar, and its population.
